title: Borel pairs and root pairings under a central isogeny
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a reductive $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], meaning smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means unipotent matrices in a faithful representation at geometric points. Let $H$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type, and let $q:H\to G$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel $K$. Faithfully flat means that $F[G]\to F[H]$ makes scalar extension exact and detects zero modules; finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra; central means commuting after every scalar extension. Then $H$ is reductive. Borel pairs (a split maximal torus and a Borel subgroup containing it), unipotent radicals, the projections $p:B\to T$, $p_H:B_H\to T_H$, and roots and coroots are as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For every Borel pair $(B,T)$ of $G$ there is a Borel pair $(B_H,T_H)$ of $H$ with $q^{-1}(T)=T_H$, $q^{-1}(B)=B_H$, and $K\subseteq T_H$. The restrictions $T_H\to T$ and $B_H\to B$ are faithfully flat. The unipotent radicals map isomorphically and the projections satisfy $p\circ q=q|_{T_H}\circ p_H$. Pullback $q_T^*:X^*(T)\to X^*(T_H)$ identifies the roots and the positive and simple roots for these pairs and satisfies$$\langle q_T^*\lambda,\alpha_H^\vee\rangle=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle.$$For $H=Z\times_F S$, where $Z$ is a split torus and $S$ is semisimple, the lifted pair has the form $T_H=Z\times T_S$, $B_H=Z\times B_S$ with a Borel pair in $S$; the roots and coroots are those of $S$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 18.18 (inverse image Borel and quotient flag variety); Corollary 17.84 (centre in every maximal torus); Definitions 23.1--23.2 and Propositions 23.4--23.5 (central isogenies induce root data with q(alpha)=1). Product and Borel decompositions: 21.29--21.35, 21.60 and proof of 23.13.

proof.text: Let $N\subseteq H$ be any smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Factor $q|_N$ through its faithfully flat image $I\hookrightarrow G$ using [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image]. By [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image], $I$ is smooth, connected, normal and unipotent. Reductivity of $G$ gives $I=1$, so $N\subseteq K$ scheme-theoretically. On coordinate rings this is a quotient $F[K]\twoheadrightarrow F[N]$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $F[N]$ is finite-dimensional.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400, image argument.

proof.text: Smoothness makes $F[N]$ reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Finite vector-space dimension makes it Artinian: a strictly descending chain of ideals strictly decreases dimension. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product]; each residue field is $F$ by clause 1 of [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing]. Thus $F[N]\simeq F^s$. The identity gives $s>0$; connectedness excludes $s>1$, since coordinate idempotents would disconnect its spectrum. Hence $N=1$. As $N$ was arbitrary, $H$ is reductive.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 19.14, printed p.400, finite smooth connected subgroup is trivial; reduced Artinian algebra expansion.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-quotient-borel-torus-images], choose a maximal torus $T_H\subseteq H$ mapping faithfully flatly onto the prescribed $T$. Every element of the central subgroup $K$ centralizes $T_H$, so [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] gives $K\subseteq T_H$ on all test algebras. Now if $h\in q^{-1}(T)(A)$, locally for a faithfully flat extension choose $t\in T_H$ with $q(t)=q(h)$. Then $ht^{-1}\in K\subseteq T_H$, so $h\in T_H$ locally and hence globally, since membership in a closed subgroup descends (its defining ideal vanishes after a faithfully flat extension only if it vanishes). Consequently $q^{-1}(T)=T_H$ scheme-theoretically. The torus is split since $F$ is algebraically closed.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, printed pp.357--358; Proposition 17.61 and Corollary 17.84, printed pp.372,379; inverse-image equality by local lifts.

proof.text: By step 3, $K\subseteq T_H$ on all test algebras, so $K$ is a closed subgroup scheme of the split torus $T_H\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. As $K$ has finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable] gives $K\simeq D(M)$ for a finite abelian group $M$. Thus $q$ is a multiplicative isogeny in the explicit sense of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-isogeny-borel-comparison]. Apply that node to get $B_H=q^{-1}(B)$ a Borel and $B_H\to B$ faithfully flat with kernel $K$. Since $T_H=q^{-1}(T)$, $T_H\subseteq B_H$, so this is the desired Borel pair. In particular [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] applies to both pairs.

source.place: Definition 18.1 and proof of Proposition 18.18, printed pp.387,391; the kernel lies in the lifted torus by step 3 (17.84).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-isogeny-root-power-laws] to $q:(H,T_H)\to(G,T)$. Centrality gives $e_\gamma=1$ for every root $\gamma$ of $H$. Thus for the corresponding root $\alpha$ of $G$, $q_T^*\alpha=\gamma$, $q_T\circ\gamma^\vee=\alpha^\vee$, and $q:U_\gamma\to U_\alpha$ is an isomorphism: in root coordinates it is $a\mapsto c_\gamma a$ with inverse $a\mapsto c_\gamma^{-1}a$. Since $B_H=q^{-1}(B)$, [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] puts every positive root subgroup in the relevant unipotent radical. Thus a positive $\gamma$ maps into $B$, so its isomorphic root subgroup has nonzero tangent weight $\alpha$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, making $\alpha$ positive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Conversely, if $\alpha$ is positive, $U_\gamma$ lies in $q^{-1}(B)=B_H$, so its tangent weight $\gamma$ is positive. Hence positive roots correspond. Pullback carries the target simple-root base to an integral basis of the source root span, and every source positive root has nonnegative integer coordinates in this basis, by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] and the root bijection. Compare this basis with the source simple-root base: each is a nonnegative integer combination of the other. Substituting these expressions in a basis vector forces its coefficient $1$ to come from exactly one coefficient $1$, all other coefficients being $0$. Thus the two bases coincide, so simple roots correspond.

source.place: Proposition 23.5, printed pp.485--486; Proposition 23.4, printed p.484; root containment in 21.29, printed p.434.

proof.text: Enumerate the positive roots of $G$ and use the corresponding enumeration for $H$. The two multiplication maps of [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] identify $U_H$ and $U$ with the ordered products of their root subgroups. Because $q$ is a homomorphism, its restriction between these coordinates is exactly the product of the root-subgroup isomorphisms from step 5. Hence $q|_{U_H}:U_H\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ is a scheme isomorphism and, being a homomorphism, a group-scheme isomorphism. For every $A$-point write uniquely $b_H=u_Ht_H$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Then $q(b_H)=q(u_H)q(t_H)$ with $q(u_H)\in U(A)$ and $q(t_H)\in T(A)$. The projections therefore give $p(q(b_H))=q(t_H)=q_T(p_H(b_H))$ on every test algebra.

source.place: Theorem 21.68(a),(b), printed p.445; Proposition 23.5, printed pp.485--486.

proof.text: For every $\lambda\in X^*(T)$ and corresponding $\gamma=\alpha_H$, step 5 gives an equality of characters of $\mathbf G_m$: $(q_T^*\lambda)\circ\gamma^\vee=\lambda\circ q_T\circ\gamma^\vee=\lambda\circ\alpha^\vee$. By the definition of the integer character-cocharacter pairing in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], their exponents agree. Thus $\langle q_T^*\lambda,\alpha_H^\vee\rangle=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ for arbitrary characters, not only for roots.

source.place: Definition 23.1 and Proposition 23.5, printed pp.483,485--486; pairing by composition.

proof.text: Now suppose $H=Z\times_F S$. The central subgroup $Z\times1$ centralizes $T_H$, so [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] puts it in $T_H\subseteq B_H$. Apply [lem-sfb-quotient-borel-torus-images] to the projection $H\to S$: its images $T_S$ and $B_S$ are a maximal torus and a Borel, with $T_S\subseteq B_S$. For either $J=T_H$ or $B_H$, a point $s$ of its image lifts faithfully flat locally to $(z,s)\in J$; multiplying by $(z^{-1},1)\in J$ gives $(1,s)\in J$. This descends because $J$ is closed. Thus $J=Z\times\operatorname{pr}_S(J)$ scheme-theoretically, proving both product formulas.

source.place: Corollary 17.86, printed pp.379--380; Proposition 17.20, printed pp.357--358; product special case of the decomposition in the proof of Lemma 23.13, printed p.489.

proof.text:

The nonzero weights and the positive weights are therefore exactly the roots and positive roots of $S$, extended trivially across $Z$.
